landmarks.name: Laurier Library
facts: It holds about a million print volumes.

landmarks.name: Dag Hammarskjold Residence
facts: It is named after a UN Secretary-General who was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize after his death.

landmarks.name: Martin Luther University College
facts: It is the university's Lutheran-affiliated college and seminary.
It began in 1911 as the Evangelical Lutheran Theological Seminary of Eastern Canada, the root of the university itself.

landmarks.name: Lazaridis Hall
facts: It is named after the co-founder of BlackBerry.
The business school moved into it in 2016.

landmarks.name: Frank C. Peters Building
facts: It is named after a former president of the university.

landmarks.name: John Aird Centre
facts: It is home to the Faculty of Music and the Maureen Forrester Recital Hall.

landmarks.name: Arts Building
facts: Ontario Premier Leslie Frost attended its opening on September 7, 1953.

landmarks.name: Centre for Cold Regions and Water Science
Theatre Auditorium
facts: It is one of the Faculty of Music's two performance spaces, alongside the Maureen Forrester Recital Hall.

landmarks.name: Fred Nichols Campus Centre
facts: It is run by the students' union and is home to the Turret nightclub.

landmarks.name: Athletic Complex
facts: It has three gyms, two squash courts, an Olympic-size swimming pool and a climbing wall.
